args.sql:
-- Check what percentile-based performance categories might look like
-- Let's see the distribution of bncrate and ctrval
SELECT 
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY bncrate) as median_bnc,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ctrval) as median_ctr
FROM sessions;

WITH session_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        s.seshkey,
        u.typelabel,
        u.seglabel,
        s.bncrate,
        s.ctrval,
        s.bncrate * (1 - s.ctrval / 100.0) AS sbra
    FROM sessions s
    JOIN users u ON s.userel = u.userkey
),
percentiles AS (
    SELECT 
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY bncrate) AS bnc_median,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ctrval) AS ctr_median
    FROM session_stats
),
session_with_perf_cat AS (
    SELECT 
        ss.*,
        CASE 
            WHEN ss.bncrate <= p.bnc_median AND ss.ctrval >= p.ctr_median THEN 'High Performance'
            WHEN ss.bncrate > p.bnc_median AND ss.ctrval < p.ctr_median THEN 'Low Performance'
            ELSE 'Mixed Performance'
        END AS perf_category
    FROM session_stats ss
    CROSS JOIN percentiles p
),
grouped AS (
    SELECT 
        typelabel,
        seglabel,
        perf_category,
        COUNT(*) AS session_count,
        AVG(bncrate) AS avg_bounce_rate,
        AVG(ctrval) AS avg_ctr,
        AVG(sbra) AS avg_sbra
    FROM session_with_perf_cat
    GROUP BY typelabel, seglabel, perf_category
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 10
)
SELECT 
    typelabel,
    seglabel,
    perf_category,
    session_count,
    ROUND(avg_bounce_rate::numeric, 4) AS avg_bounce_rate,
    ROUND(avg_ctr::numeric, 4) AS avg_ctr,
    ROUND(avg_sbra::numeric, 4) AS avg_sbra
FROM grouped
ORDER BY typelabel, seglabel, perf_category;
